classification.difficultyReason: Infer whole secant lengths from the equal triangle sides, form a product equation and calculate the perimeter.

content.prompt: An equilateral triangle is partly obscured by a circle. The lengths of the visible segments are indicated on the diagram. Find the perimeter of the triangle.

spec.description: Upright equilateral triangle with its three middle side portions hidden by a structural white circular mask. Upper visible side segments are 1 each, lower visible side segments 2 each, and visible base segments 3 each.
spec.mathematics: The construction uses an equilateral coordinate frame and a circle whose side intersections leave the six specified visible segments. Coordinates are construction data, not additional printed givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Hidden edges and the unknown total side length are not shown.

answer.short:
$21$.

For side length $x$, the secant rule gives $2(x-1)=3(x-3)$, so $x=7$ and the perimeter is $3x=21$.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the side length of the equilateral triangle. From either lower vertex, the sloping secant has external length $2$ and whole length $x-1$; the base secant has external length $3$ and whole length $x-3$. By the Power of a Point Theorem,
$$\begin{align*}2(x-1)&=3(x-3)\\2x-2&=3x-9\\x&=7.\end{align*}$$
Therefore the perimeter is
$$\begin{align*}P&=3x\\P&=3\times7\\P&=21.\end{align*}$$
